expressions.dx1: (1 - exp(-(x1/gateSpeed)**2))*(bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2 - visc*exp(Min(Max(-dampSlope*y, -expCap), expCap))*x1 - fric*tanh(x1/velScale)) + exp(-(x1/gateSpeed)**2)*(((bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2) - staticForce + sqrt(((bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2) - staticForce)**2 + softWidth**2))/2 - (-(bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2) - staticForce + sqrt((-(bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2) - staticForce)**2 + softWidth**2))/2 - stickRate*x1)

parameters.name: bias
parameters.description: `bias` is the constant acceleration offset. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: rest
parameters.description: `rest` is the amplitude of the odd sinusoidal restoring term. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: visc
parameters.description: `visc` is the positive baseline velocity damping coefficient. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: gain
parameters.description: `gain` is the linear input coefficient. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: freq
parameters.description: `freq` is the inverse-state frequency inside sine and cosine. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: fric
parameters.description: `fric` is the magnitude of saturating moving-velocity damping. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: velScale
parameters.description: `velScale` is the velocity width of the hyperbolic tangent transition. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: dampSlope
parameters.description: `dampSlope` is the state dependence of positive exponential velocity damping. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: even
parameters.description: `even` is the coefficient of the even cosine-minus-one restoring correction. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: staticForce
parameters.description: `staticForce` is the force threshold of the low-speed static branch. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: gateSpeed
parameters.description: `gateSpeed` is the velocity width of the Gaussian low-speed gate. Estimated jointly in the final free-run output-error fit on both supplied files, from the training-only starting value reported in estimation.

parameters.name: expCap
parameters.description: `expCap = 40` is a chosen dimensionless numerical safety cap for the exponential argument. It prevents overflow far beyond observed states; it is inactive over all fitted and screened trajectories. It is not inferred physical saturation.

parameters.name: stickRate
parameters.description: `stickRate = 100` 1/s is the chosen low-speed velocity decay rate, equal to the inverse of the supplied `T_s = 0.01` s. This regularizes zero-speed sticking without discontinuous sign switching and gives a decay scale of one sample; it is not fitted.

parameters.name: softWidth
parameters.description: `softWidth = 0.1` V/s is a chosen acceleration smoothing width for the static-force dead zone. It is small relative to acceleration fluctuations in data/train.csv, and avoids non-differentiability of an exact positive-part operator. It is not fitted or an independently observed physical constant.

estimation.criterion: Sum of squared free-run errors in `y` at every within-trajectory row after its initial sample, with equal weight per sample. This matches the scored output and long-run simulation requirement rather than optimizing the noisy centered derivative target. Errors have unit Y and the minimized sum has unit Y**2.
estimation.data: Final coefficient estimation uses data/train.csv (all trajectories, all 3522 rows) and data/val.csv (all trajectories, all 1192 rows), with each initial row used solely to initialize simulation. No rows or trajectories are otherwise omitted. Structural screening first fits training data only and evaluates all validation trajectories without resetting the states; final refitting then uses both files to exploit all available experiments. Consequently final validation-file errors are in-sample, not new held-out evidence. The file names, sample counts and row roles are as supplied in TASK.md.
estimation.method: Classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta with `T_s = 0.01` s and `x2` held at the preceding logged sample is used, with measured initial states and no subsequent state replacement. Every trajectory is separate. SciPy `scipy.optimize.least_squares` uses trust-region reflective bounded nonlinear least squares, linear loss, two-point finite-difference Jacobians, Jacobian-based parameter scaling, `max_nfev = 350`, and `ftol = xtol = gtol = 1e-10`; the last four are dimensionless numerical settings. This method handles the small bounded nonlinear output-error problem directly; derivative least squares alone is insufficient because centered differentiated, quantized measurements need not be instantaneous acceleration. Numba only accelerates the deterministic RK4 calculations. No random numbers or seeds are used. All fitted parameters listed in this candidate are re-estimated together in one final step on both files. They start from this family's preceding training-only simulation least-squares fit, whose numerical values are: `bias = 3.660098422394763` V/s; `rest = 109.4172444240855` V/s; `visc = 1.790755057601655` 1/s; `gain = 27.7335382121618` V/(s*U); `freq = 1.044212174745626` 1/Y; `fric = 20.10707050248031` V/s; `velScale = 0.2775650970261364` V; `dampSlope = 0.2086023120098605` 1/Y; `even = 4.097485266820294` V/s; `staticForce = 10.57632378050441` V/s; `gateSpeed = 0.195216472916054` V. These warm starts were chosen because the preliminary fit already tracked the measured trajectories. The final optimization bounds are `-10 <= bias <= 10` V/s; `1 <= rest <= 300` V/s; `0.05 <= visc <= 30` 1/s; `1 <= gain <= 100` V/(s*U); `0.4 <= freq <= 1.6` 1/Y; `0 <= fric <= 60` V/s; `0.12 <= velScale <= 5` V; `-1 <= dampSlope <= 1` 1/Y; `-30 <= even <= 30` V/s; `0 <= staticForce <= 50` V/s; `0.06 <= gateSpeed <= 2` V. Bounds keep damping positive, constrain plausible local restoring and forcing magnitudes, and avoid unresolved velocity transitions; they are search restrictions, not established physical limits. All moving width, static threshold and gate-width parameters are fitted in this candidate. The static smoothing and low-speed decay are fixed regularization assumptions, not estimated coefficients. The earlier training-only search and its initial values are reproducible in the scripts stated in origin. `reproduce_candidates.py` reproduces the final joint step from the exact numerical training-fit starting values. References: the SciPy reference documentation for `scipy.optimize.least_squares` describes the trust-region reflective method; Steven H. Strogatz, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos, is a general oscillator reference. These bibliographic references are cited from memory; attempted web checking returned no usable content, so neither source was verified online in this round. Neither reference establishes the identity or physics of this undisclosed system.

discussion.interpretation: Units are not supplied. In this record, Y denotes the unknown unit of `y`, V the unknown unit of `x1`, U the unknown unit of `x2`, and s seconds; these are unit placeholders, not expression symbols. The numerical relation `dy = x1` is assumed from within-trajectory centered differences, implying compatible numerical scaling V = Y/s, not a known physical calibration. The expressions use only the logged states and input; the column `dx1` is not an argument. The complete acceleration is `(1 - exp(-(x1/gateSpeed)**2))*(bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2 - visc*exp(Min(Max(-dampSlope*y, -expCap), expCap))*x1 - fric*tanh(x1/velScale)) + exp(-(x1/gateSpeed)**2)*(((bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2) - staticForce + sqrt(((bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2) - staticForce)**2 + softWidth**2))/2 - (-(bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2) - staticForce + sqrt((-(bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2) - staticForce)**2 + softWidth**2))/2 - stickRate*x1)`. Here `bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2` is the net state/input force before damping, with constant, odd, even and input effects as their parameter descriptions define. `exp(-(x1/gateSpeed)**2)` tends to one near zero velocity and zero away from zero; it blends branches rather than switching discontinuously. The moving branch is `bias - rest*sin(freq*y) + even*(cos(freq*y) - 1) + gain*x2 - visc*exp(Min(Max(-dampSlope*y, -expCap), expCap))*x1 - fric*tanh(x1/velScale)`. In the static branch, the two square-root positive-part approximations implement a smooth force dead zone of threshold `staticForce`; `softWidth` smooths its corners. `-stickRate*x1` rapidly decays low velocity. `gateSpeed` sets the near-zero-velocity band, not an extra state. `velScale` is the separately fitted moving-damping width. The model may reduce low-force creep but is not exact sticking because its smoothing is finite. `dy = x1` remains the kinematic equation.
discussion.origin: Centered-difference inspection motivated kinematics, and residuals.py showed measured low-speed plateaus at different state values: smooth moving friction alone allowed unwanted creep. fit_extended.py therefore compared a smooth force dead zone, a Gaussian static/moving blend, Stribeck damping, asymmetric friction and a discontinuous low-speed model. The Gaussian blend was retained as a distinct, continuously evaluable family; its gate and regularizing low-speed decay are guessed approximations motivated by plateau residuals, not observed physical states. fit_final.py added the empirically supported even trigonometric force and positive exponential damping and jointly estimated the model. The static branch was not produced by symbolic-regression software. More complex harmonic and nonlinear-input models did not justify inclusion in this pool.
discussion.limitations: Units are not supplied. In this record, Y denotes the unknown unit of `y`, V the unknown unit of `x1`, U the unknown unit of `x2`, and s seconds; these are unit placeholders, not expression symbols. The numerical relation `dy = x1` is assumed from within-trajectory centered differences, implying compatible numerical scaling V = Y/s, not a known physical calibration. The expressions use only the logged states and input; the column `dx1` is not an argument. Physical identity, calibrated units, independent measurement noise, hidden actuator dynamics and friction memory are unknown. The derivative columns are centered finite differences, not independent acceleration measurements. Training coverage is approximately `-2.514 <= y <= 2.536` Y, `-20.107 <= x1 <= 14.452` V and `-4.946 <= x2 <= 3.954` U, computed from data/train.csv and rounded outward. There is no guarantee outside this support or beyond the supplied trajectory durations. In particular, the asserted kinematic equation does not resolve quantization or initial-velocity error.  Static threshold, gate width and moving-friction smoothing are partly interchangeable; there are no independent friction or force measurements. The narrow fitted Gaussian gate may be weakly resolved by sampling, and different starts gave modestly different low-speed parameter values. One grouped cross-validation fold reached its allowed function-evaluation count, so superiority over the simpler model is not claimed. True hysteretic friction needs an additional memory state which this two-state model cannot contain. Fixed low-speed decay and square-root smoothing are numerical modeling assumptions.
